title: Defined bacterial consortium highlights the impact of intestinal bacteria on DNA methylation and tumorigenesis.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and read Additional file 1 (393 KB .docx) from the publisher: Table S1 has exactly 7 data rows (7 genes), and 4 of those 7 have no methylation value at all ('—'). Queried NCBI for each deposited project: the RRBS (reduced representation bisulfite sequencing, a method that measures DNA methylation at CpG sites) project PRJNA1370025 contains 13 sequencing runs, the RNA sequencing project PRJNA1365758 contains 21, and the 16S ribosomal RNA gene survey PRJNA1168567 contains 48. A search of GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus, NCBI's processed-data repository) for these projects returned 0 records, so no processed count matrix or methylation coverage table was deposited anywhere.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Per-group animal numbers (germ-free n=3, C13-DSMZ n=3, C13-UM149 n=5 for methylation; germ-free n=6, C13-DSMZ n=3, C13-UM149 n=5 for expression), the analysis pipeline (TrimGalore, Bismark to the mm9 mouse genome, methylKit, ComBat-seq, edgeR), and the statement that samples were merged by group before differential methylation testing. I did not download any raw sequencing reads (project rules forbid it).

a1_downloadable.note: The three NCBI Sequence Read Archive projects are public with no login or access application. But they hold only raw sequencing reads; no processed table is deposited (GEO search returned 0 records), and project rules forbid downloading raw reads.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. There is no label column anywhere in the released data. Any target (per-CpG methylation fraction, gene expression, differential methylation) would have to be built from raw reads by running read trimming, Bismark alignment to the mouse genome, and methylKit, i.e. reconstructing the paper's entire pipeline before a single row of a feature/label table exists.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. Inputs are also absent as features: there is no per-sample methylation matrix, no gene count matrix, and no 16S species-abundance table. Only compressed raw reads. The one table I opened (Table S1) has 5 numeric columns for 7 genes.

a4_units_stated.note: Where numbers do exist they are labelled: Table S1 states percent promoter methylation, mean log2 CPM (counts per million) expression, log fold change, and false discovery rate. Units are not the problem here.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, badly. The only released table has 7 rows. The biological unit is the mouse: 11 animals in the methylation arm (3 germ-free, 3 C13-DSMZ, 5 C13-UM149) and 13 RRBS sequencing libraries total, which I counted in NCBI. The checklist floor is ~1,500 labelled rows (~400 for classification).

a6_fits_laptop.note: FAIL. To get any usable table you would have to align raw RRBS and RNA-seq reads (13 + 21 libraries, tens of GB of FASTQ) to the mm9 mouse genome with Bismark and bowtie2 — days of CPU time and well over the 5 GB working-set limit, for 11 mice of output.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Counts are consistent: 13 RRBS runs in NCBI matches the 11 mice plus tumour/normal splits described, and Table S1's legend (n=3 and n=4) matches the 7 differentially expressed genes named in the text. Nothing disagrees — the numbers are simply tiny.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance is clean and physical: methylation from bisulfite sequencing, expression from RNA sequencing, tumour counts from macroscopic dissection. No other model's output is used as a label. A8 is not why this fails.

existing_models.name: DeepCpG (convolutional and recurrent neural network predicting CpG methylation from local DNA sequence plus neighbouring methylation states)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported as substantially more accurate than prior methods for single-cell methylation state prediction; evaluated on mouse embryonic stem cells profiled by single-cell bisulfite sequencing and single-cell RRBS, held-out CpG sites. I read the abstract and repository description, not the full benchmark tables.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Did not retrieve the discussion section, so I cannot quote what they named as unsolved.

existing_models.name: DeepMethylation (deep learning framework combining a sequence convolutional module with an epigenomic annotation module for tissue-specific methylation prediction)
existing_models.score_and_split: Published in PLOS Computational Biology for tissue-specific methylation status prediction and functional variant annotation; I saw the abstract only and did not record its metric or split.

integration.join_key: Mouse gene symbol or mm9 genome coordinates would in principle join to mouse methylation atlases, but with 7 released rows and 11 animals there is nothing to join.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: the released data carries no per-sample matrix to bring to a partner resource.

controls.positive_control: The paper's own biology offers one in principle (the colibactin-producing strain must show more tumours and more DNA damage than the low-activity strain), but with 3 to 5 mice per group there is no held-out set to test it on.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is meaningless at n=11 animals.
controls.external_validation: No second independent dataset of defined-consortium mouse methylation exists that I found.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model claim is available: with 11 mice, 13 methylation libraries, samples merged by treatment group before testing, and only 7 genes released as a table, any model would be describing one experiment in one mouse strain in one facility rather than predicting anything.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use gut bacterial consortium membership to predict which gene promoters gain or lose DNA methylation in mouse colon tumours.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on, for each CpG site or gene promoter, its surrounding mouse DNA sequence plus which of two defined 13-species bacterial consortia colonised the mouse. Verified example count: 7 rows in the only released table; 11 mice; 13 methylation sequencing libraries.
plain_idea.predict: Output would be the percent methylation at that promoter, or whether it is differentially methylated. The true answer comes from reduced representation bisulfite sequencing, which chemically converts unmethylated cytosines so that the fraction of methylated copies at each CpG can be counted from sequencing reads.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Researchers studying how specific gut bacteria drive colon cancer would want to know which promoters a given microbe silences, so they could pick targets for follow-up experiments. As released, the data cannot support that.

more_or_better_data.why: DeepCpG was trained on single-cell bisulfite data covering many thousands of CpG sites across many cells; this paper releases 13 bulk sequencing libraries from 11 mice and one 7-row summary table.

confidence_score.why: With 3 to 5 mice per group, and with samples merged by group before the published differential test, there is no replicate structure left to estimate per-prediction uncertainty.

models_beatable.why: DeepCpG (2017) is open and runnable, but beating it is irrelevant here because this dataset provides no training set; the obstacle is data volume, not the strength of the incumbent.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: our model would not see everything the baseline sees plus more, because this paper contributes no usable processed methylation matrix at all.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict promoter DNA methylation change from mouse DNA sequence conditioned on which defined bacterial consortium colonised the animal, with a convolutional sequence model or a DNA language model as the backbone. The data cannot support it.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because Part A failed before a task was defined. Building any table would require aligning 34 raw sequencing libraries to the mouse genome, which is days of CPU time and is forbidden by the project's no-raw-reads rule.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows in the only released table and the number of sequencing runs in the NCBI projects. I did both: 7 rows, and 13 methylation runs from 11 mice. That killed it in two commands.

verdict_reason: A beautifully controlled germ-free mouse experiment, but as an ML substrate it is a hard reject on three killers at once. A5: the only released table, which I opened, has 7 rows, and the biological unit is a mouse — 11 of them, 13 methylation libraries, which I counted in NCBI. A2 and A3: no processed matrix was deposited anywhere (GEO returned 0 records for all three projects), so both the features and the label would have to be reconstructed from raw reads by rerunning the authors' Bismark and methylKit pipeline. A6: that reconstruction is tens of GB of FASTQ and days of CPU time, and project rules forbid downloading raw sequencing data. The paper is honest about the underlying limit itself — it states that no statistically significant methylation-to-expression associations were detected due to limited sample size and effect size, and that 4 of its 7 differentially expressed genes had insufficient CpG coverage to test. Nothing about the files contradicts the paper; the experiment is simply three-to-five mice per arm, which is a fine mouse study and not a dataset.
